tagline: An online free-for-all deathmatch in Foundry Nine, a freight yard and assembly hall linked by doors, a service lane and a covered maintenance route.
overview:
RedDM is a compact online first-person deathmatch, one of the first standalone games built on RedEngine. Its map, Foundry Nine, joins an open freight yard and a covered assembly hall through offset doors, an outdoor service lane and a covered maintenance route, with loading bays at each end and freight containers, pallets and screens for cover.

One player hosts and the others join. Once at least two players are ready, an eight-minute round begins: everyone for themselves, first to 30 kills wins, then results and a rematch. You start with a rifle and can cycle through the bat and the engine's eleven firearms. Movement is deliberately tactical: no extra sprint speed, quick acceleration and strong friction. The map is still a greybox: plain shapes, no textures.
story: No story: RedDM is a straight arena deathmatch, built to put the engine's online play, hit detection and movement through their paces. Foundry Nine is an industrial yard with nobody working in it but the players.
goal: Be the first to 30 kills in an eight-minute round (free for all).
rules: A round needs at least two ready players (the lobby shows who is ready).
Every kill scores one; first to 30, or the most kills when eight minutes are up, wins.
You respawn after a death at one of six spawn points behind the loading and dispatch screens.
Everyone starts with a rifle; the mouse wheel cycles the bat and the other firearms.
Players can join a round already in progress.

Known problem: the version on this site was built with an engine that no longer accepts this game's revolver setting (the engine removed the revolver on 2026-09-28), so it very likely refuses to start. The in-game pictures here were drawn without that one setting.
